title: Turn a last write wins edit into a 409 with @Version
summary: Optimistic locking does not stop an overwrite across two screens until the version makes a round trip, and only some operations may retry.

turns.user: product edit screen: two admins open the same product and save one after the other, the second save just overwrites everything. the first persons changes vanish silently. want an error instead

assistant.body: Perfect use case for JPA optimistic locking. With @Version on Product, Hibernate adds where version = ? to every update and bumps the version by one. If someone else updated the row first, zero rows match and Spring translates that into ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException. Map that exception to 409 Conflict in a @RestControllerAdvice and concurrent saves no longer silently overwrite each other.

turns.user: tried it. opened the product on screen A and B, saved A, then saved B. B got a normal 200 and As changes are gone

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous explanation was incorrect. @Version compares against the version loaded inside the same transaction. B's PUT loads the product again within its own request, so it picks up the version A just wrote and nothing conflicts. All it protected was the short gap inside a single request. The version the screen was opened with has to go to the client and come back with the save, and the service compares the two. Assigning request.version() to the entity does not help, because Hibernate compares against the value it loaded, so the check is explicit. The version also only moves on flush, so the response has to be built after a flush. Otherwise it returns the old number and the second save from the same screen gets a 409.

sed -i '' -e 's/int price)/int price, long version)/' -e 's/product\.getPrice())/product.getPrice(), product.getVersion())/' src/main/java/com/example/product/UpdateProductRequest.java src/main/java/com/example/product/ProductResponse.java

turns.user: ok 409 works now. but stock reservation updates the same Product and during a sale its 409s everywhere. cant we just retry

assistant.body: Whether a retry is safe depends on what the operation bases its value on. Reserving stock subtracts from the current stock every time, so reading again and redoing it gives the right result. The edit screen must not retry. It would write values a person chose from a stale screen onto the newest row, which is last write wins all over again. Note: the exception is thrown at commit, after the method returns, so a loop inside the @Transactional method never sees it. A separate bean outside ProductService calls reserve again, each time in a fresh transaction, up to three times.
